title: Restore shared beads project state
description: The repository currently ignores local .beads/.dolt state and bd reports an empty default embedded database despite project docs and ralph/progress.txt referencing prior waluau-* issues. Decide and implement the shared beads storage/sync setup so bd ready/list shows the real project queue for every contributor.
design: Treat issue tracking as production infrastructure. Do not leave an empty local default embedded database as the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: bd prime no longer warns about missing beads configuration; bd ready/list operate against the intended shared project database; documented sync instructions match the actual storage model; beads state is pushed to its remote.

title: Resolve documented V0 syntax gaps in parser and typechecker
description: docs/design/0002-language-v0.md says V0 includes unary numeric negation, boolean not, and if / elseif / else, and it says expression statements are only valid for calls. The current implementation does not tokenize or parse elseif or not, has no unary expression support, and accepts any parsed expression as a statement without enforcing the call-only rule (see crates/waluau-parser/src/lib.rs and crates/waluau-hir/src/lib.rs). Either implement these forms or narrow the design doc so the documented language matches reality.
design: Treat the design doc as the contract for V0. If a construct stays out of scope, remove it from the accepted language note; otherwise add parser, AST, type-checking, and tests together.
acceptance_criteria: elseif, unary -, and unary not are either implemented end-to-end with tests or explicitly removed from docs/design/0002-language-v0.md; the compiler rejects non-call expression statements with a focused diagnostic; parser/typechecker tests cover both accepted and rejected forms.

title: Align V0 surface syntax with Luau-style function/local/operator forms
description: The accepted V0 design doc presents a Lua-like surface syntax and uses Luau-style forms such as function, local, : return annotations, and word logical operators in examples, while the current lexer/parser/fixtures accept a different ad hoc surface: fn, let, ->, and &&/||. Compare docs/design/0002-language-v0.md, the implementation in crates/waluau-lexer/src/lib.rs and crates/waluau-parser/src/lib.rs, and Luau's published grammar at https://luau.org/grammar/. Decide which surface syntax is intentional for Waluau and make the docs, fixtures, lexer, parser, and diagnostics converge on that choice. Random drift is the problem here, not merely having a smaller subset than Luau.
design: Keep deliberate semantic deviations, but make surface syntax decisions explicit and internally consistent. Prefer following Luau/Lua spellings unless there is a documented reason to diverge.
acceptance_criteria: A design decision exists for function declarations, local declarations, return-type annotation spelling, and logical operator spelling; docs and examples match the implementation; fixtures and parser tests cover the chosen syntax; unsupported alternate spellings fail with clear diagnostics instead of silently defining a competing dialect.

title: Bootstrap Rust toolchain in Vercel build
description: The Vercel production build for the playground fails on main because rustup is present but the stable toolchain is not installed in the build environment. Update the repo build path so Vercel installs the required stable toolchain and wasm32 target before running the workspace wasm build.
design: Keep the fix in the checked-in build script so Vercel and any other clean build environment use the same bootstrap path.
acceptance_criteria: Vercel playground builds no longer fail with missing stable toolchain; the repo build command bootstraps the required Rust toolchain and wasm target in Vercel; local validation still passes.
close_reason: Updated the repo wasm build script to install the stable Rust toolchain and wasm32 target before building, which fixes Vercel's missing-toolchain failure.

title: Connect Vercel Git integration for playground
description: The waluau-playground Vercel project exists, is linked locally, and has a successful production deployment, but vercel git connect git@github.com:hybrist/waluau.git failed because the Vercel GitHub integration does not currently have access to the repository or org. Grant access and connect the repo so pushes and PRs trigger deployments automatically.
design: Keep the project root at repository root and rely on the checked-in vercel.json build settings once Git integration is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Vercel GitHub integration has access to hybrist/waluau; the waluau-playground project is connected to that repository; pushes to main create production deployments; pull requests create preview deployments.

title: Connect Vercel Git integration for playground
description: The waluau-playground Vercel project exists, is linked locally, and has a successful production deployment, but  failed because the Vercel GitHub integration does not currently have access to the repository or org. Grant access and connect the repo so pushes and PRs trigger deployments automatically.
design: Keep the project root at repository root and rely on the checked-in vercel.json build settings once Git integration is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Vercel GitHub integration has access to hybrist/waluau; the waluau-playground project is connected to that repository; pushes to main create production deployments; pull requests create preview deployments.

title: Set up Vercel deployments for playground
description: Configure the repository so the playground app deploys on Vercel from this monorepo. Use a build setup that can compile the Rust wasm artifact and publish the Vite output for apps/playground, then create or link the Vercel project and verify a deployment works.
design: Prefer a repo-root Vercel config so builds can access the Rust workspace directly and publish apps/playground/dist without relying on Vercel root-directory settings outside version control.
acceptance_criteria: Repo contains Vercel configuration for the playground deployment; Vercel project is linked or created against this repository; at least one deployment succeeds; deployment workflow is documented in-repo.
close_reason: Added repo-root Vercel configuration, linked the project, and verified a successful production deployment at waluau-playground.vercel.app. Follow-up for Git-triggered deployments is tracked separately.

title: Add GitHub Actions for playground and Rust checks
description: Add GitHub Actions workflows that validate the apps/playground frontend and the Rust workspace on pull requests. Cover Node setup and playground lint/build, plus Rust fmt, clippy, tests, and the wasm build path used by the playground. Create and merge a PR once checks are green.
design: Keep CI explicit and split by concern so failures are easy to diagnose. Reuse the existing root build:wasm script for the browser artifact path instead of inventing a separate CI-only command.
acceptance_criteria: GitHub Actions exist for playground and Rust validation; local validation covers the same commands; a PR is opened with those changes; PR checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented GitHub Actions for playground and Rust checks and opened PR #4 with passing checks.

title: Design M2 array syntax, typing, and wasm-gc representation
description: Write the design note for M2 arrays before implementation. Capture source syntax, element typing rules, bounds behavior, allocation semantics, mutation model, and the initial wasm-gc representation.
design: Make representation choices explicit before adding parser/type/codegen surface area.
acceptance_criteria: A docs/design note exists for arrays; it states included/excluded operations; it defines type-checking rules and diagnostic expectations; it identifies the concrete Wasm GC constructs or fallback plan to use first.

title: M2 arrays and initial wasm-gc representation
description: Start the next feature-ladder milestone after scalar v0: add arrays and the first heap-backed wasm-gc representation work. This should force decisions around array syntax, typing, allocation, runtime representation, and Wasm GC emission without pulling in tables/metatables yet.
design: Follow docs/design/0001-overview.md: arrays are the first heap-backed feature and the first wasm-gc pressure test.
acceptance_criteria: Design note captures array syntax, element typing, allocation model, and wasm-gc representation; implementation tasks exist for frontend, HIR typing, IR representation, codegen, runtime/browser exposure, and end-to-end tests; tables/metatables remain explicitly out of scope.

title: Implement usable CLI compile command
description: waluau-driver::run currently returns Ok(()) and the waluau-cli binary exits successfully without compiling input. Add command-line behavior for compiling a source file through the existing pipeline and writing wasm output or diagnostics.
design: Keep orchestration in waluau-driver and keep waluau-cli as the thin process entrypoint.
acceptance_criteria: CLI accepts an input .walu path; successful compile writes wasm bytes to a requested output path or a documented default; invalid programs print diagnostics and exit non-zero; behavior is covered by tests or a focused integration check.

title: Harden IR verifier to match design contract
description: docs/design/0003-ir-cfg-ssa.md requires CFG and SSA verification for predecessor/successor consistency, dominance, phi consistency, operand types, branch bool conditions, and return type matching. The current verifier mostly checks duplicate values, undefined uses, and block existence.
design: Prefer explicit value-type inference and dominator helpers over ad hoc checks buried in lowering.
acceptance_criteria: Verifier checks phi input count/order against predecessors; uses are dominated by definitions including phi edge semantics; binary/cast/call operands have expected concrete types; branch conditions are bool; return values match function return type; negative tests cover each invariant.

title: Extend playground with function calling view tab
description: Extend the playground with a new tab on the right that renders a function calling view. It lists exported functions from the compiled WASM module and allows specifying inputs, running the functions, and displaying results. Updates inputs change immediately.
close_reason: Completed implementation, styling, linter, tests, and builds successfully.

title: Migrate repo to shared Beads worktree setup
description: Align this repository's Beads layout with the new shared worktree support so all git worktrees resolve to the main repo's .beads database instead of materializing isolated per-worktree databases.
close_reason: Migrated local Beads setup to shared-worktree layout by untracking .beads from git, ignoring it repo-wide, disabling auto-export in the local config, and redirecting the existing worktree to the main repository database.

title: Update compiler playground: restore IR, show WAT, maximize layout
description: Restore the IR layout in compiler playground, render WAT text instead of binary Wasm bytes, and utilize full available screen width by removing huge margins
close_reason: Completed: Restored intermediate representation (IR), added Wasm Text (WAT) tab using wasmprinter, and maximized screen layout width

title: Set up pnpm monorepo with apps/playground and Rust WASM compiler integration
description: Create a pnpm monorepo, implement wasm compilation for the compiler driver, and build a two-column React-based playground in apps/playground to type-check and dump the IR.
close_reason: Successfully set up pnpm monorepo, Rust WASM compiler target, and two-column React playground under apps/playground

title: Implement array frontend and HIR typing
description: Add parser, AST, and HIR/type-checking support for the M2 array slice after the design note lands.
design: Keep arrays distinct from Lua tables; do not add dynamic table semantics under the array feature.
acceptance_criteria: Parser accepts the chosen array syntax; HIR validates element types and rejects unsupported operations clearly; tests cover valid arrays, type mismatches, and out-of-scope Lua table syntax.

title: Lower arrays through IR and wasm-gc codegen
description: Extend IR and Wasm code generation for the M2 array representation selected in the design note.
design: Keep heap representation details localized to IR/codegen boundaries with tests that expose behavior, not implementation trivia.
acceptance_criteria: IR models array allocation/access/mutation as needed by M2; Wasm output validates; generated programs execute under an engine configuration that supports the selected wasm-gc features; negative cases produce diagnostics instead of invalid Wasm.

title: Add end-to-end array execution fixtures
description: Add fixture-backed execution coverage for M2 arrays across compiler driver tests and playground-visible examples.
design: Use fixture files as the reusable source of truth for examples and execution tests.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover array creation and at least one read/write or length operation from the M2 design; Wasmtime or equivalent execution tests assert runtime results; playground examples include a valid array program; ./check passes.

title: Move driver inline test programs into fixtures
description: crates/waluau-driver/src/lib.rs contains sizable inline Waluau source strings for Wasmtime execution tests. Move those programs into fixture files so test cases are reusable by the CLI, playground, and future integration tests.
design: Keep Rust tests focused on pipeline assertions and keep source programs in fixtures/*.walu.
acceptance_criteria: Inline multi-line Waluau programs in waluau-driver tests are replaced with include_str! fixtures; fixture names describe behavior; existing Wasmtime execution coverage remains equivalent; any newly added fixtures are surfaced consistently with existing fixture conventions.

title: Replace Wasm block-dispatch lowering with structured control flow
description: The current scalar Wasm backend validates and executes, but it lowers CFG blocks through a synthetic program-counter local and dispatch loop. Replace this with structured Wasm control-flow emission where feasible, or document the cases that still require dispatch.
design: Keep Wasm stack-machine concerns inside waluau-codegen-wasm; do not leak structured Wasm constraints back into the IR API unless a design note justifies it.
acceptance_criteria: Generated WAT for simple if/while programs uses structured block/loop/if control flow rather than a full function-level pc dispatch loop; existing Wasmtime execution tests still pass; any irreducible or unsupported CFG shapes have clear diagnostics or documented fallback behavior.

title: Integrate Wasm code generation into playground
description: The playground currently compiles source to IR text via the browser-facing waluau-wasm crate, while the native driver already lowers the same pipeline to executable Wasm bytes through waluau-codegen-wasm. We are ready to track the playground integration work because the codegen backend exists, the driver tests exercise emitted Wasm successfully, and the browser crate builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown. The remaining work is to switch the playground-facing API and UI from IR dumping to codegen output presentation and any browser-side handling needed for the emitted bytes.
design: Prefer the smallest change that keeps parser, type checker, IR builder, and wasm emitter aligned with the existing driver pipeline. Reuse waluau-codegen-wasm from waluau-wasm rather than reimplementing emission logic in JavaScript.
acceptance_criteria: The playground uses the codegen pipeline instead of stopping at IR construction. The browser-facing wasm API returns codegen output in a form the UI can consume. The playground UI presents the generated Wasm output and surfaces codegen errors cleanly. The integration is covered by appropriate automated tests or verification steps.

title: Confusing error when local binding shadows typed parameter
description:
Reproduction:

```lua
fn add(x: number) -> number
    let x: u64 = 20
    return x
end
```

The current diagnostic for this code is confusing. The snippet appears to trigger an error around re-binding `x` inside the function body and/or the returned type no longer matching the declared `number` return type, but the reported message does not clearly explain the real problem.

Expected behavior:
- The compiler should emit a direct, actionable diagnostic.
- If shadowing a parameter is invalid, say that explicitly and point at the `let x` binding.
- If shadowing is allowed, the diagnostic should clearly explain the return type mismatch (`u64` returned from a function declared to return `number`).

Acceptance criteria:
- The issue includes this exact repro snippet.
- The desired diagnostic behavior is documented clearly enough for follow-up implementation/testing.
close_reason: Implemented direct shadowing diagnostic for parameter/local rebinding, added regression test, and verified with ./check

title: Add numeric cast syntax and implicit widening conversions
description: Add numeric conversion semantics for the integer and float scalar types. The language should allow implicit widening conversions where the destination can represent the full source range, for example i32 -> i64 and i32 -> f64. Narrowing or potentially lossy conversions must require explicit cast syntax using `x :: T`, for example `x :: i32` when `x` is i64 should truncate to fit into i32. Scope includes parser support for cast syntax, type-checking rules for implicit widening versus explicit narrowing, and backend lowering that matches the specified truncation and extension semantics.
design: Keep the implicit rules small and predictable: only permit conversions that are clearly widening and non-lossy under the chosen scalar model. Require `::` for truncating or otherwise lossy numeric conversions so call sites stay explicit.
acceptance_criteria: The parser accepts `expr :: Type` cast syntax; the type checker accepts implicit widening conversions such as i32 -> i64 and i32 -> f64; lossy conversions such as i64 -> i32 require an explicit cast; code generation implements the documented extension and truncation behavior; tests cover both accepted and rejected conversion cases.

title: Track precise 64-bit integer literal representation
description: Now that i64 and u64 are accepted types, the frontend should stop representing all numeric literals as f64 so full-range 64-bit integer literals can be parsed and validated precisely. The current implementation accepts i64/u64 types but only guarantees exact integer literal handling within the f64-safe integer range.

title: Add i64 and u64 scalar types
description: Extend the explicit numeric scalar type support to include i64 and u64 in the language, type checker, IR, docs, and tests. number should remain an alias for f64.

title: Centralize examples into shared fixtures
description: Move compiler example programs into a central fixtures location in the repository. Use those fixture files as the source for full-file tests and for the web playground instead of duplicating inline source snippets. The playground should dynamically discover available fixtures with Vite glob imports so new fixtures appear automatically without manual registration.
design: Prefer a single canonical fixture directory with a stable file extension for Waluau source files. Keep fixture loading minimal: Rust tests can read files directly, while the playground should use import.meta.glob or equivalent Vite-supported discovery. The implementation should avoid maintaining separate fixture registries for test and web consumers.
acceptance_criteria: A shared fixtures directory exists for example programs; full-file tests load compiler inputs from those fixture files; the playground loads available fixtures dynamically via Vite globs instead of a hard-coded preset list; at least one fixture is exercised by both tests and the playground; duplicate inline example definitions are removed where practical.
close_reason: Implemented shared .walu fixtures, fixture-based driver tests, and Vite glob discovery in the playground

title: Add proper numeric scalar types
description: Replace the current effectively-single numeric type model with explicit numeric scalar types suitable for Wasm code generation. The language currently exposes `number` and `bool`, with `number` implemented as `f64`, but scalar Wasm needs a deliberate type system that can represent integer and floating-point widths directly. Introduce first-class numeric types such as `u32`, `i32`, `f32`, and `f64` (and any other core scalar types we decide to support), while continuing to accept `number` as an alias for `f64` for source compatibility and convenience. Update the frontend, typed representations, IR assumptions, docs, and tests so numeric operations are typed against the concrete scalar kinds rather than a generic `number`.
design: Make numeric types explicit in the source language and internal representations instead of baking in a generic `number` abstraction. Preserve `number` only as a parser and type alias for `f64`, not as a distinct semantic type. Align the language with Wasm scalar types so codegen can choose the correct instructions without ad hoc reinterpretation later. Resolve the current design and implementation mismatch where docs describe `i32` but the implementation only supports `number` and `bool`.
acceptance_criteria: The language accepts explicit numeric scalar types including at least `u32`, `i32`, `f32`, and `f64`; `number` remains accepted as an alias for `f64`; type checking and IR distinguish numeric kinds precisely; docs describe the supported numeric types and alias behavior; tests cover parsing, type checking, and representative arithmetic and comparison behavior across the supported scalar types.

title: Add wasm codegen placeholder scaffold
description: Introduce an explicit wasm codegen entrypoint signature that accepts IR modules and returns bytes, plus a crate-local smoke test that locks in the current placeholder diagnostic until real lowering lands.

title: Pass Ralph instructions as direct prompt
description: Update ralph/run so the contents of ralph/RALPH.md are used as the opencode run message instead of a wrapper prompt that tells the agent to read the file.

title: Switch Ralph runner to opencode CLI
description: Update ralph/run so the relay loop invokes the OpenCode CLI instead of Claude, preserving the existing non-interactive streaming behavior as closely as possible.

title: Add repo-root check script
description: Add an executable repo-root check script that validates the Rust workspace is in a good state, including formatting and compilation-oriented checks, using the project's existing cargo tooling.

title: Add initial Wasm code generation
description: Lower scalar CFG+SSA functions to Wasm, validate emitted modules, and execute end-to-end tests. This milestone should cover numeric operations, direct calls, branches, loops, and returns before any wasm-gc-backed heap features.
design: Start with plain scalar Wasm to isolate frontend and IR correctness. Add wasm-gc-backed runtime features later, beginning with arrays.
acceptance_criteria: Scalar programs compile to valid Wasm and pass execution tests for arithmetic, branching, and loops.

title: Implement CFG and SSA IR
description: Lower typed HIR into a conventional control-flow graph IR and add SSA construction with verification. Cover mutable locals, branches, loops, phi insertion, dominance, and textual dumps/tests.
design: Use a traditional block-based SSA design with phi nodes. Keep Wasm stack-machine details out of IR and add verifiers early to avoid debugging invalid states.
acceptance_criteria: A typed HIR function lowers to CFG, SSA form can be constructed and verified, and tests cover merge and loop phi cases.

title: Implement frontend for language v0
description: Implement the first compiler frontend slice for the strict Lua-like v0 language: lexer, parser, AST, name resolution, and type checking for numbers, booleans, typed locals, typed functions, control flow, and calls.
design: Keep Lua-like syntax but do not inherit dynamic Lua semantics. Conditions are bool-only, all locals and function signatures are explicitly typed, and unsupported features should be rejected clearly.
acceptance_criteria: The compiler parses and type-checks the v0 subset with diagnostics and tests for valid and invalid programs.

title: Capture compiler architecture docs
description: Write in-repo design documentation for the Waluau compiler bootstrap. Capture the monorepo workspace layout, crate responsibilities, language v0 scope, CFG+SSA IR design, verifier invariants, milestone ordering, and early test strategy.
design: The docs should freeze early decisions so implementation can proceed without re-litigating repo layout or IR direction. Favor direct, implementation-facing guidance over aspirational architecture language.
acceptance_criteria: docs/design contains overview, language v0, and CFG+SSA design notes; docs describe the crates/ workspace layout, strict typed Lua-like v0 semantics, milestone ladder, and verification expectations.

title: Scaffold Cargo workspace under crates
description: Create the initial Cargo workspace layout at the repository root with crates/ for the compiler components. Add the initial crate set and wire a no-op CLI through the driver so the monorepo shape is stable before feature work begins.
design: Prefer a stable monorepo shape now over a later repository reshuffle, but keep crates thin and avoid infrastructure-only abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: A root Cargo workspace exists with crates/ members and a buildable CLI-to-driver path; crate boundaries match the documented architecture closely enough to avoid moving files later.

title: Bootstrap Waluau compiler
description: Create the initial architecture, docs, and implementation plan for a Lua-like compiler targeting Wasm. This issue tracks the overall bootstrap effort, including monorepo layout, language v0 scope, CFG+SSA IR direction, and phased feature rollout through arrays, strings, tables, metatables, and modules.
design: Use a Cargo workspace with crates/ from day one. Start with a strict statically typed Lua-like subset. Use AST -> typed HIR -> CFG -> SSA -> Wasm. Defer wasm-gc object features until after scalar codegen works end-to-end.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture decisions are captured in-repo; follow-up implementation tasks exist for workspace scaffolding, frontend, IR, and codegen; the initial plan clearly distinguishes v0 scalar compilation from later wasm-gc-backed runtime features.

title: Add tables
description: Design and implement tables after arrays and strings are established. Define the supported table model precisely before implementation, including key types, indexing semantics, mutability, equality, and any split between record-like and dynamic behavior.
design: Do not smuggle in full Lua table semantics accidentally. Decide intentionally whether the first table model is typed, dynamic, or staged.
acceptance_criteria: Table semantics are documented and implemented with tests covering the supported key and mutation behavior.

title: Add bytes and strings
description: Add byte-oriented and string types after arrays are available. Define representation, mutability, equality, indexing behavior, and any required runtime helpers before implementation.
design: Do not let string work accidentally choose table or module semantics. Freeze representation and equality rules before codegen work.
acceptance_criteria: Bytes and strings have documented semantics, end-to-end implementation, and tests for representation-sensitive behavior.

title: Add arrays as first wasm-gc heap feature
description: Design and implement typed arrays as the first heap-backed feature after scalar Wasm code generation is working. This includes array representation, creation, indexing, update operations, bounds behavior, and backend support using wasm-gc.
design: Arrays are the first intentional wasm-gc milestone because they force heap representation decisions without pulling in full table semantics too early.
acceptance_criteria: Typed arrays are supported end-to-end with clear semantics, tests, and a documented wasm-gc representation.

title: Add require and modules
description: Add a module system and require-style loading after the core language and runtime model are stable. Define whether modules are linked statically or loaded dynamically, module singleton semantics, dependency behavior, and compile-time versus runtime responsibilities.
design: The module system should be designed intentionally instead of falling out of string or table implementation details.
acceptance_criteria: Module semantics are documented and implemented, with tests covering dependency loading and repeated imports.

title: Add metatables
description: Add metatables only after the table model is stable. Define exactly which operations consult metatables, how dispatch behaves, and how metatable semantics constrain optimization and static reasoning.
design: Metatables are late by design because they infect operation semantics and optimizer assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: Supported metatable behavior is documented and implemented with tests that cover dispatch and fallback behavior.
